pros: 7 schools within 500m of Yau Tong Industrial City — highest school density found
Yau Tong Industrial City has units from 1,848-3,880 sqft at just HK$9.8-10.5/sqft — cheapest per-sqft industrial rent in Kowloon

35,000+ households in immediate public housing estates — captive afterschool market

golden_zone_thesis: Yau Tong is the single highest-conviction golden zone. It combines the cheapest industrial rent in Kowloon ($9.8/sqft) with the densest school cluster (7 schools within 500m), massive public housing (35,000+ households), and a dual-line MTR interchange. No boxing gym exists within 1km. The business model is airtight: 3:30-6pm afterschool kids from 7 nearby schools + Lam Tin estates, 12-2pm office workers from Kwun Tong (5 min MTR), 6-9pm adults from the housing estates. Saturday family classes pull from TKO via the interchange line. This is a first-mover opportunity in a market with zero direct competition and captive demand.

pros: 6 schools within 500m walk of Kwun Tong Industrial Centre
MASSIVE office worker population (80,000+) for lunchtime classes — highest of any candidate

golden_zone_thesis: Kwun Tong is the proven model. It already has fitness businesses operating in industrial buildings, proving the DMC/OC barrier is surmountable. The triple pipeline is strongest here: 80,000 office workers for lunch, 6 nearby schools for afterschool, 40,000 households for evening. The key differentiator vs Yau Tong is the office lunch crowd — Yau Tong doesn't have this. Kwun Tong's risk is slightly higher rent and existing competition. But the market is so large that even 1% capture rate = 4,000 potential customers. A dedicated kids boxing + adult boxing gym with no direct kids boxing competitor within 500m is a clear gap. The 18ft ceiling gym listing at Kwun Tong Industrial Centre suggests landlords are actively seeking fitness tenants.

golden_zone_thesis: Tuen Mun is the highest-volume, lowest-cost play. With zero boxing gyms serving 500,000 people and 73 schools, it's a blue ocean. The business model shifts: lower price point but massive volume. $100/kid/month × 100 kids = $100k/month revenue. Industrial rent at $10/sqft means a 1,000 sqft gym costs $10k/month — leaving huge margin. Risk is lower-income demographic and distance from central HK. But no competition means you own the market. This is the 'start cheap, dominate early' play. Saturday classes pull from entire Tuen Mun/Yuen Long/Tin Shui Wai corridor via Tuen Ma Line.

golden_zone_thesis: San Po Kong is the 'professional image' play. New Tech Plaza offers a modern, Grade A industrial building environment that appeals to middle-class parents who want their kids in a 'nice' facility. The school density is excellent (6 schools within 500m), and Diamond Hill's dual MTR interchange means catchment extends to Ma On Shan, Tuen Mun via Tuen Ma Line, and Kowloon East via Kwun Tong Line. The downside is higher rent and a 10-min MTR walk. But for parents driving, parking in San Po Kong industrial buildings is easier than Kwun Tong. This is the premium positioning play within the golden zone strategy.

golden_zone_thesis: Tsuen Wan is the balanced play — decent schools, decent offices, decent rent, decent transport. It doesn't dominate any single dimension but scores well across all. The presence of private housing with higher-income parents (Vision City, Bellagio) allows premium pricing for kids classes. The Tuen Ma Line connection means catchment extends to Tuen Mun/Yuen Long in 15-20 minutes. Less of a 'first-mover absolute monopoly' than Yau Tong or Tuen Mun, but a solid market with proven demand.

golden_zone_thesis: Kwai Chung is the ultra-budget play. At $7/sqft, a 1,000 sqft gym costs only $7,000/month — making it viable even with very low class prices ($60-80/kid/session). The Kwai Chung Estate's 35,000 residents provide a built-in market. But the economics rely on volume and very tight margins. Limited lunchtime revenue. Best as a second location once the brand is established, or as a pure afterschool-only model. The buy option at $1.5-2.5M is genuinely interesting — owning the unit eliminates rent risk.
